pages.name: NPC Interactions
pages.html:
NPC Interactions: NPC interactions are used to determine how an NPC responds to the spacers, by setting the difficulty of interactions with them and the Skill checks necessary for doing so.

Book p.56

pages.name: Determining NPC Demeanour
pages.html:
Determining NPC Demeanour: Roll the following table to determine an NPC’s demeanour when interacting with them.

2DNPC reaction
2Hostile (-2DM)
3-5Rude (-1DM)
6-8Indifferent (+0DM)
9-11Intrigued (+1DM)
12+Agreeable (+2DM)

Once the demeanour of the NPC(s) is determined, apply the DM to all interactions with the spacer.

Book p.56

pages.name: Generating NPC
pages.html:
Generating NPC: If needed, use this generator to make a notable NPC.

  • Most NPCs you interact with will be just getting by and oftentimes have a career. This table is meant for NPCs that the spacers want to interact with in depth or if they encounter one while exploring.
  • Rumours and Information: NPCs can be interacted with to gain actionable information. Use the Rumour generator to determine any rumours or information the spacers can gain from the NPCs.
  • Hostile NPCs: Hostile NPCs generated on other encounter tables have their own table on pg. 59 That table includes specific stats for the NPCs in those encounters.
  • Non-hostile NPCs: most NPCs are not immediately hostile and as such, will be generated using the NPC table.
  • NPCs hits: If needed, assume all NPCs have END 7. All NPCs will only have a single weapon on them as allowed by the Law level. If desired, the referee can roll 1D: 1-3) Unarmed 4-5) blade 6) gun.

Use the following table to generate any random NPC the spacer may come across. When the rules state that the d66 roll is modified, any DM is applied to the tens place.

  • For example: +1 DM to a d66 will produce a range of 21-76 on the table.

The listed NPCs are described by their profession or living situation to provide flavour and as a potential lead for gathering information.

pages.name: Information & Rumours
pages.html:
Information and Rumours: NPCs can offer insight into a spacer’s current objective or offer up new pieces of information that can lead to new opportunities. All information gathering requires succeeding on an applicable Skill check, based on who the spacer is talking to and what they want to learn.

  • Remember: Determine the NPC’s reaction first to determine interaction difficulty.

There are two types of knowledge a spacer can learn from roleplaying with NPCs:

  • Informative: Actionable knowledge the spacer can follow up on.
  • Rumours: Pieces of information that require additional digging to uncover the truth of. Rumours always lead to another NPC, location, or object that can clarify whether the rumour is true or false.

Use the following procedure when asking NPCs for information:

  • 1) Determine NPC reaction to the characters.
  • 2) Determine how much information they offer: Roll D3; result is the number of pieces of info they share.
  • 3) Determine the type of information they offer.

Information and Rumour table

1DInformation Type
1Adventure Lead: Roll 1D; 1) Person 2) place 3) thing 4) object 5) background info 6) secret.
2Narrative Information: Roll 1D; 1) Major fact 2) minor fact 3) notable fact 4) unnecessary fact 5) valuable information 6) unexpected connection.
3Job Information: Roll D3; 1) Fact about patron 2) fact about a place 3) fact about a job detail.
4Job Lead: Roll 1D; 1) Patron suggestion 2) job rumour 3) criminal patron suggestion 4) criminal job rumour 5) secret patron suggestion 6) secretive job rumour.
5Rumour: Roll 1D; 1) NPC connection 2) faction Connection 3) location connection 4) narrative clue 5) adventure clue 6) job clue.
6Local Gossip: Roll 1D; 1) Illicit information on an NPC 2) illicit info on a faction 3) illicit info on a location 4) dangerous information 5) conspiracy theory 6) unbelievable connection.
  • Adventure lead: This information leads to potential side jobs or personal interest pursuits.
  • Narrative information: This information assists or advances the spacer’s current narrative.
  • Job information: Any information that assists the spacer with their current job they may have questions about.
  • Job lead: This information can lead a spacer to a potential client or a rumoured job a patron is offering.
  • Rumour: Rumours require additional roleplaying to discern the source of the rumour or if the information offered is actionable. Use the Discernment table to determine the truth of the rumours.
  • Local gossip: Gossip is information that NPCs will share that is open-ended and may not be related to a current objective. It is essentially local flavour that may be actionable if the spacer decided to pursue it.

Book p.57

pages.name: Random NPC Encounters
pages.html:
Random NPC Starport/Settlement Encounter: The following NPCs are encountered when “random NPC” is produced on an encounter table, typically with d66 range. These encounters are assumed to be NPCs that may or may not be confrontational.

Important: Random NPC encounters don’t always involve overt violence. The spacers might be harassed, stopped and questioned by police, or mistaken for someone else.

  • When Interacted With: Use the NPC Reaction table with SOC DM applied.
  • Who: The type of person encountered.
  • Number: Roll the listed dice to determine how many appear.
  • Avoid: This represents the difficulty it takes to avoid the group. This can be done through dialogue or by evading the group. The referee decides what Characteristics and/or Skill would be applied, then they roleplay the scenario.
  • Weapon: This is the typical weapon they carry, if the Law Level allows. Criminals and police are not affected by Law Level limitations.
  • Attack: This is the DM to any attack throws they make.
  • Hits: The listed number is applied for STR, DEX, and END when determining hits.
  • Armour: The type of armor they are wearing if Law Level allows. Criminals and police are not affected by Law Level limitations.

There are a few variables that can alter the interactions:

  • Recon: Anyone keeping a lookout has a +2 to the Avoid column roll.
  • Vehicles: Any group with an asterisk will have a nearby vehicle. The vehicle will be the average kind found based on the local Tech Level.

Book p.58
